finding.expected: Preserve the selected source ID and stable URL only as the current P8 pilot/planning case. Define the reusable V1 exact-listing gate as requested target source ID versus observed/post-navigation current-product source ID: parse the requested URL with the one canonical TikTok parser, require a valid requested target, and when the page exposes an observed/current-product ID require it to match that requested target; explicit conflict, different ID, malformed/unverifiable identity, search/login/challenge redirect, or unrelated page fails closed. Do not require the implementation capability itself to hard-code source ID 1731381331718341815. Live acquisition authority must remain NONE, and the first real capture must still require HUMAN_BRAIN_LIVE_PUBLIC_PDP_PILOT_AUTHORIZATION. Tighten the governance regression to preserve this capability-versus-authorization distinction. Do not broaden fields, add live acquisition, change Product Intelligence/Product Source ownership, alter Affiliate separation, or change the unique NEXT commitment.
finding.issue: Section 6 changes the approved exact-listing identity gate from a target-versus-observed binding rule into a pilot-specific allowlist by requiring every future V1 requested ID to equal the currently selected source ID 1731381331718341815. That conflates the technical public-PDP capability with the current pilot authorization and makes the separately authorized collector implementation semantically hard-coded to one listing. TASK-231 preserves the selected P8.1 case as planning context, but its AC5/hard boundary requires the later implementation to parse the requested target and verify the observed or post-navigation listing identity fail-closed; it does not authorize source ID 1731381331718341815 to become a universal parser/admission constant. Capability is not authority: a bounded collector may be capable of validating another requested TikTok PDP while live use still remains NONE until a fresh Human/Brain live-pilot authorization.
